text:
ana: Heads up — after the kernel hotpatch last night a handful of nodes in gpu-pool-us-west1-a lost their MIG partitions. nvidia-smi reports the physical GPU but `nvidia-smi -L` shows no MIG instances.

sam: which nodes exactly? any pattern (kernel, driver version, flavor)?

ana: affected nodes: gpu-usw1-0123, gpu-usw1-0456, gpu-usw1-0789. All were on driver 535.86-1 and kernel 6.1.77-flavorX before the hotpatch. Quick dump from gpu-usw1-0123:
```
$ nvidia-smi
Tue Mar 18 12:34:10 2025
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.86       Driver Version: 535.86       CUDA Version: 12.2     |
| GPU 0: Tesla T4 (UUID: GPU-aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee)           |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
$ nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: Tesla T4 (UUID: GPU-aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee)
# no MIG instances listed
```

jia: that looks like the driver loaded but the MIG mode/profile config didn't get re-applied. Two suspects: (1) module/init ordering changed so `nvidia-mig-mgr` didn't see the device at boot, (2) udev or DKMS rebuild targeted the wrong build symlink after the kernel symlink change.

matt: FWIW I saw the cfgmgmt run log for those hosts — we accidentally changed `/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build` symlink to point at `/usr/src/linux-6.1.77-patched` instead of the distro flavor. DKMS modules likely rebuilt against the patched headers, leaving the NV driver module mismatched for the running kernel variant.

lee: confirmed — the symlink change was in the sysadmin recipe that landed in canary on friday (we missed a conditional for flavorX). That explains why only flavorX nodes hit this.

ana: quick triage steps I ran that helped in one case:
```
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced
sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm
# reapply MIG config
sudo nvidia-smi mig -i 0 -cgi 19,19,19,19 -C
```
After that one node's MIG instances reappeared in ~8s. But that's a live workaround, not a durable fix.

sam: any sign of NVML/GPU UUID mismatch with k8s device-plugin? We had a blackout last month where device IDs in kube nodes didn't line up with nvml output.

ana: yes — device-plugin labels were still pointing to old UUIDs on two nodes. `kubectl describe node gpu-usw1-0456` showed labels like `nvidia.com/gpu-uuid=GPU-1111-oooo` but nvml reports a different physical GPU UUID. I wrote a small reconcile script (ran it once) to map PCI IDs -> NVML UUID -> kube labels, but that's a bandaid.

jia: long-term fixes:
- revert cfgmgmt symlink change for flavorX ASAP
- rebuild and redeploy the DKMS packages from the correct headers, or roll driver to 535.94 which we validated on staging
- add a post-boot healthcheck that ensures `nvidia-smi -L` lists expected MIG instances and that device-plugin labels match NVML UUIDs

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for pool gpu-pool-us-west1-a -> driver 535.94 (canary first: gpu-usw1-0123)

ops-bot: incident created: INC-20250318-09 (priority: P2) — owners: @ana @lee. Notes: temporary MIG reapply command documented in runbook.

matt: I'll patch the cfgmgmt recipe to guard symlink for kernel flavors and push the DKMS rebuild job for the impacted hosts.

ana: ETA for rollback + DKMS job: ~20m. Will update here after canary passes.

sam: thanks — keep notes in the incident runbook. :thumbsup:
